skill.name: azure-resource-manager-redis-dotnet
skill.description: Guides .NET developers through Azure Resource Manager SDK workflows for Azure Cache for Redis management, configuration, and operations.
skill.summary: Manage Azure Cache for Redis resources with the .NET Azure Resource Manager SDK.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, placeholder Azure URLs, sample private IPs, and documented Azure variable names. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found. One semantic issue remains because sample code prints Redis access keys to console output.

remediation.issue: Redis access keys are printed in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Console.WriteLine calls for primary, secondary, and regenerated keys. Show masked placeholders and explain secure storage instead.

remediation.issue: The export example places a SAS token in a URL string.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that SAS tokens are secrets. Recommend secure secret storage and short-lived tokens for import and export workflows.

remediation.issue: Service principal variables are shown near credential setup.
remediation.suggestion: State that values must never be committed, logged, or included in prompts. Prefer managed identity where available.

content.user_title: Manage Azure Redis with .NET ARM SDK
content.value_statement: Provisioning Azure Cache for Redis requires many ARM SDK details. This skill guides .NET developers through Redis management workflows, security settings, and operational patterns.
actual_capabilities: Shows package setup for Azure.ResourceManager.Redis and Azure.Identity.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential authentication for ARM clients.
Outlines create, read, update, and delete workflows for Redis caches.
Covers firewall rules, patch schedules, import, export, reboot, and key rotation.
Summarizes SKU options, capacity sizes, supported resource types, and common pitfalls.
Connects management-plane provisioning with StackExchange.Redis data-plane usage.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not validate live Azure subscriptions.
It does not replace Azure RBAC review, cost planning, or production testing.
Examples use placeholder names, URLs, IP ranges, and secrets.
It focuses on Azure Cache for Redis management APIs, not Redis command design.

use_cases.title: Provision a Redis cache
use_cases.description: Plan and generate .NET ARM SDK steps for creating Azure Cache for Redis with secure defaults.

use_cases.title: Manage Redis operations
use_cases.description: Review update, delete, reboot, patch schedule, import, export, and key rotation workflows before implementation.

use_cases.title: Evaluate SDK choices
use_cases.description: Separate management-plane tasks from StackExchange.Redis data-plane tasks during architecture planning.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic cache plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the steps for creating a Standard Azure Cache for Redis with .NET. Include authentication, resource group access, and secure defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Redis configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my planned Redis SKU, TLS setting, firewall range, and tags. Point out risks and missing Azure details.

prompt_templates.title: Design operational workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design .NET ARM SDK workflows for patch schedules, key rotation, import, export, and force reboot. Include safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare management and data planes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to explain which tasks belong in Azure.ResourceManager.Redis and which belong in StackExchange.Redis for my application design.

output_examples.input: Create a secure Azure Redis cache for a .NET service.
output: Authentication plan using DefaultAzureCredential and a subscription resource.
Recommended cache creation steps with TLS 1.2 and non-SSL access disabled.
Notes about SKU selection, tags, and long-running ARM operations.

output_examples.input: I need to rotate Redis access keys safely.
output: A key rotation sequence for primary or secondary keys.
Warnings to avoid logging secrets or storing keys in source files.
Follow-up tasks for updating dependent connection strings.

output_examples.input: Should I use Azure.ResourceManager.Redis or StackExchange.Redis?
output: Use Azure.ResourceManager.Redis for provisioning and management actions.
Use StackExchange.Redis for application data operations such as reads and writes.
Use both when an application needs infrastructure setup and Redis command access.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and Azure RBAC instead of hardcoded credentials.
Disable non-SSL access and set TLS 1.2 or later for Redis caches.
Treat access keys, SAS tokens, and connection strings as secrets in every example.
anti_patterns: Do not print Redis access keys or connection strings to console output.
Do not use placeholder IP ranges or blob URLs without environment review.
Do not use management-plane SDK calls for normal Redis data operations.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps generate and review .NET Azure Resource Manager SDK guidance for Azure Cache for Redis management tasks.

faq.question: Does it manage Redis data keys and values?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Azure management APIs. Use StackExchange.Redis for Redis data operations.

faq.question: Which authentication approach does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends DefaultAzureCredential so local, managed identity, and service principal flows can work without hardcoded secrets.

faq.question: Can it choose the right Redis SKU?
faq.answer: It can explain SKU tradeoffs and feature requirements. You must still validate cost, capacity, and production requirements.

faq.question: Can it configure firewall rules?
faq.answer: It can guide firewall rule creation and deletion through the ARM SDK. Review every IP range for your network policy.

faq.question: Is it safe to copy every example directly?
faq.answer: No. Replace placeholders and avoid logging secrets before using examples in a real application.
